clue.text: Fiddle Swiatek carelessly holds the wrong way round

indicators.note: the held letters must be read from right to left, so they appear backwards in the clue
the phrase Swiatek carelessly holds the answer within its run of letters

explanation.surface: A tennis star carelessly holds her racket the wrong way round, as if fiddling with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' hides the letters TEKCAR across 'Swiatek carelessly', and 'the wrong way round' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a swindle or scam, the same as a fiddle in British slang.

clue.text: Dry balls with containers set aside for removal

indicators.note: the containers are the outermost letters holding the rest, and setting them aside drops them

parts.note: arid means dry
balls are formal dances

explanation.surface: Someone drying tennis balls puts their tubs aside to clear them away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with containers set aside' removes the outer letters A and S from ARIDDANCES.
explanation.definitionFit: Riddance is the act of getting rid of something, a clearing out or removal.

clue.text: Playing Dart, score appeared on screen as equal

indicators.note: playing with the letters of these words moves them into a new order

explanation.surface: A darts player's score shows up on a TV screen during the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' tells you to rearrange DART and SCORE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors who costarred shared top billing in a film or show, appearing as equals.

clue.text: Before the end of Wimbledon, no.1 lady quits

indicators.note: the first piece is placed before the next in the answer

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible story

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A top-ranked woman player walks out before the Wimbledon final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quits' is not a verb here but the adjective, as in 'we're quits'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quits means neither owes the other anything, so the two sides are level.

clue.text: Super shot by Halep, perhaps during golf

parts.note: a smash is an overhead tennis shot, of the kind a player such as Simona Halep might play
in means during, as in 'in the night'
G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tennis star plays a superb shot, oddly in the middle of a round of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashing is informal British praise meaning excellent or super.

clue.text: Rearing sheep, maybe Raducanu gets an Italian sheepdog

indicators.note: in a down clue rearing lifts the word upward, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
Emma Raducanu, the British tennis player

explanation.surface: A tennis star raising sheep acquires an Italian dog to guard them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rearing' looks like farming but reverses RAM to MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maremma is a white Italian breed of guard dog used with flocks of sheep.

clue.text: Guaranteed some tennis this month — ace!

parts.note: a set is a part of a tennis match
inst., short for instant, means this month in old business letters
an ace counts as one

explanation.surface: Someone is promised some tennis this month and is delighted: ace!
explanation.walkthrough: INST (instant) is a dated commercial abbreviation for the current month.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set in stone is fixed and cannot change, so it is assured.

clue.text: A bit of ice regularly calms Brit's feet

indicators.note: a single bit taken from the word, here its first letter
regularly means taking every other letter of these words

explanation.surface: A piece of ice soothes a British person's aching feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'calms Brit' give AMBI. 'feet' are units of verse, not body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambs are metrical feet in poetry, an unstressed syllable then a stressed one; iambi is the Latin plural.

clue.text: Spinning ball goes to and fro, two completing rally

parts.note: GO followed by the same word coming back gives GO then OG

indicators.note: the two letters that complete the word, its last two

explanation.surface: A ball spins back and forth across the net in a rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to and fro' is GO, then GO the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a googly is a deceptive delivery from a leg-spinner that turns the opposite way to expected.

clue.text: Obvious soft shot crossing net returned

indicators.note: the shot word straddles the other, so it sits inside

parts.note: a pat is a gentle tap

indicators.note: returned means the word is turned back to read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, then reversed

explanation.surface: A gentle shot clears the net and is sent back over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' looks like the ball going over the net, but it means the soft shot straddles the reversed net.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means plain to see or evident.

clue.text: Son gripped by awful double faultiness

indicators.note: the son letter is held inside the following word

parts.note: dire means awful
a pair is a double, two alike

explanation.surface: A player's son is gripped by a dreadful double fault on court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' reads as a double fault, but it supplies PAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Disrepair is a broken-down, poorly maintained state, so things are defective.

clue.text: Beat me with top shot

indicators.note: shot as in ruined or wrecked, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An opponent defeats me with a top-class shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like a tennis stroke but tells you to rearrange ME and TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the pace or rhythm of music, its beat.

clue.text: Nadal retiring? Nowhere near

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Rafa is the nickname of Rafael Nadal

explanation.surface: Is Nadal retiring? Not even close.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means far away, at a great distance, not anywhere close.

clue.text: Grassy knoll where shots seen as dear chap fell?

parts.note: hen is a Scottish and northern English term of endearment, like dear
a man is a chap
a fell is a hill in northern England

explanation.surface: A grassy mound where a dear chap fell, as if a shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: HENMAN HILL is the slope at Wimbledon where fans watch matches on a big screen, named after British player Tim Henman.
explanation.definitionFit: The bank at Wimbledon is a grassy mound where fans see shots broadcast on a large screen.

clue.text: Fresh clothes, going into fifth?

definitions.meaning: a change of gear, gear being clothes, read the other way round
moving a car into fifth is shifting gear

explanation.surface: A player puts on fresh clothes, perhaps before the fifth set.
explanation.definitionFit: Shifting a car into fifth is a gear-shift; a new set of togs is a change of gear too.

clue.text: Roof's opening in Centre Court, perfect

indicators.note: the roof letter goes inside the centre word

parts.note: the core is the centre

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The opening of the roof on Centre Court at Wimbledon is perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfect' is a verb here: to put right.
explanation.definitionFit: To perfect something is to put it right, removing every fault.

clue.text: Watching players all in white swear

parts.note: being at a match is watching it
Test cricket, where the players wear whites

explanation.surface: Spectators watch players dressed all in white, then cuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At Test' means watching a Test match, in which cricketers wear all-white kit.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to declare something true, often under oath.

clue.text: Isn't Swiss legend here, asks Spooner in gap between flights

indicators.note: Spooner's question swaps the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: the question about Tell not being present is 'Where's...?'
William Tell, the legendary Swiss archer, asked after here

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a Swiss legend is present, in the space between stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Asking 'Where's Tell?' because he isn't here; swap the W and ST sounds to get STAIR WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A stairwell is the vertical shaft that a staircase runs through, the space between flights.

clue.text: Allow cut grass to cover lines, with terrible consequences

parts.note: let means allow

indicators.note: the grass word covers the lines, holding them inside

parts.note: hay is cut and dried grass
L is short for line, so two lines give LL

explanation.surface: Letting the mown grass cover the court lines has dire results.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethally means in a deadly way, so the outcome is fatal or devastating.

clue.text: Favourite evidently embarrassed by fuss

parts.note: ado means fuss
red as in red-faced

explanation.surface: The tournament favourite is clearly flustered by all the fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places ADO beside RED.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourite is plainly someone loved and cherished, so adored fits it.

clue.text: Rising protégé male seed encourages to advance

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word reads from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: a ward is someone under another's protection
a son is a male offspring, seed meaning descendants

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming seeded young male player is urged on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seed' sounds like a tournament ranking but means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw someone on is to lure or lead them forward.

clue.text: Good uniform English grass reflected in edge of cutter?

parts.note: U is Uniform in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: reflected as in a mirror, so the word appears backwards

parts.note: a lawn is an area of grass

explanation.surface: Neat English grass is mirrored at the edge of a mower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' reverses E plus LAWN to give NWALE. 'cutter' is a small boat, not a mower.
explanation.definitionFit: The gunwale is the upper edge of a boat's side, and a cutter is a kind of boat.

clue.text: Stars meeting for sport with unknowns

parts.note: a gala is a sports meeting, such as a swimming gala
x and y are unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: Star players gather at a tournament alongside some unknowns.
explanation.definitionFit: A galaxy is a vast system of stars.

clue.text: Ram and Salisbury's first defeats

parts.note: to stuff is to ram or cram

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A ram and Salisbury's opening defeats, as if a sports results line.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff an opponent is informal for beating them heavily.

clue.text: It's logical that Boulter flourished, missing nothing

indicators.note: flourished as in waved about, so the letters are thrown about
missing means these letters must be left out of the jumble

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Harriet Boulter, a British tennis player, flourished, just missing a zero score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flourished' rearranges THAT BOULTER and 'missing nothing' takes out an O.
explanation.definitionFit: A truth table is a chart used in formal logic to list a statement's values.

clue.text: Perfect club for a gentle hit on grass, no pressure

indicators.note: no means the pressure letter is removed

parts.words: club for a gentle hit on grass
parts.note: a putter is the golf club for gentle strokes on the green
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A golfer's ideal putter, used with no strain at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter means complete or absolute, as in utter nonsense.

clue.text: Post-war reminder of triumph in pre-war Championships

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of these words

explanation.surface: A memento of victory in the Championships before the war, kept after it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Championships is the formal name for Wimbledon.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumphal arches were built to commemorate victories in war.

clue.text: Mate's instruction to keep very quiet between rounds

indicators.note: the quiet letters sit between the two rounds

parts.note: O is round in shape, so two rounds give OO
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction to play very quietly

explanation.surface: A friend tells someone to stay silent between rounds of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppo is British slang for a friend or colleague, a mate.

clue.text: Initially three love in games, Osaka's big cushion

indicators.note: these letters go inside the games word

parts.note: fun and games

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Naomi Osaka leads three games to love while sitting on a big cushion.
explanation.walkthrough: Osaka is also a Japanese city, pointing to a Japanese item.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a Japanese padded mattress, effectively a large cushion.

clue.text: Ladies' Draw or Men's Draw?

parts.note: ladies or men is one's sex, and draw means appeal, so the draw of each sex

explanation.surface: A tennis question: the women's bracket or the men's?
explanation.walkthrough: A draw is also an attraction, and Ladies' or Men's names a sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical attractiveness is the allure, or draw, of one sex for the other.

clue.text: McEnroe's method perhaps drove Evans crazy, wanting call out overturned

indicators.note: crazy means the letters run wild into a new order
overturned means the word is turned over, so read backwards

parts.note: to yell is to call out

explanation.surface: McEnroe's style drove Evans mad, not least his line calls being overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges DROVE EVANS; 'overturned' reverses YELL.
explanation.definitionFit: John McEnroe was famous for serving and rushing to the net, the classic attacking tennis tactic.
